approved_premise.override_reason: For the first Episode, establish the protagonist's cartographer role, mentor relationship, world navigation logic, and the first Main Saga anomaly. The Luna-selected fisher premise remains a strong later world-side candidate but gives a 12-year-old apprentice too much community route-safety responsibility too early.

premise.title: The Angle That Wouldn't Match
premise.logline: A routine beacon calibration turns into Deniz's first real test of whether patient observation can outweigh a mentor's doubt.
premise.protagonist_role: Apprentice surveyor conducting supervised but semi-independent beacon calibration checks.
premise.immediate_objective: Confirm whether a magnetic-stone beacon reading at Beacon Ridge is a genuine anomaly or an instrument error before the calibration window closes.
premise.inciting_event: While logging a routine reading, Deniz notices the beacon's angle has drifted further than tide tables allow, but the harbor's shipping logs show no confirming delays or complaints that would prove the drift is real.
premise.central_problem: Deniz has only a single suspicious reading and a narrow window before the tide changes and the anomaly becomes unmeasurable again, with no corroborating evidence yet and a mentor likely to dismiss a lone data point.
premise.wonder_or_discovery: A pattern emerges suggesting the drift is tied to tidal extremes rather than random error, hinting at something systematic in the old navigation network.
premise.stakes: If dismissed as a measurement mistake, a real anomaly worth investigating could go unrecorded for another season; if reported too early on thin evidence, Deniz risks being seen as overconfident and losing supervised field privileges.
constraints: Limited daylight and tide window at Beacon Ridge
Only supervised access to the beacon instruments
Mentor evaluates methodology, not just conclusions
premise.meaningful_choice_pressure: Deniz must decide whether to report the single unusual reading now, risking dismissal for insufficient evidence, or spend the remaining tide window trying to capture a second corroborating reading, risking losing the anomaly's window entirely if it doesn't recur.
premise.mystery_or_forward_question: Is this drift an isolated fluke, or the first visible sign of a larger disagreement between the old markers and the official charts?
premise.local_payoff: Deniz secures at least a provisional, logged acknowledgment of the anomaly, changing how the mentor treats future field reports.
persistent_outcomes_possible: Mentor's assessment of Deniz's methodology shifts (skeptical, cautious-respect, or dismissive)
A dated logbook entry becomes a reusable reference item
A rumor begins circulating among harbor navigators about 'the ridge beacon problem'
world_specific_elements: harbor shipping logs as corroborating evidence

dimensions.name: PREMISE_MATURITY
dimensions.description: Core story problem should feel substantively suitable for a 12-year-old, not like preschool play dressed in harder vocabulary.

dimensions.name: NARRATIVE_COMPLEXITY
dimensions.description: Support layered goals, changing information, reversals, and multi-step progression while remaining readable.

dimensions.name: CONCEPTUAL_COMPLEXITY
dimensions.description: Allow systems, evidence, competing explanations, responsibility, trust, and consequences without requiring adult-only abstraction.

dimensions.name: CAUSAL_DEPTH
dimensions.description: Important outcomes should follow from multiple linked causes rather than one-step problem-solution patterns.

dimensions.name: INFERENCE_DEMAND
dimensions.description: Reader should sometimes connect clues, motives, patterns, or consequences without every relationship being stated directly.

dimensions.name: AGENCY_COMPLEXITY
dimensions.description: Character should face meaningful options, trade-offs, strategy, or uncertainty; choices must not be predetermined.

dimensions.name: STAKES_CONSEQUENCE_COMPLEXITY
dimensions.description: Actions should matter to reputation, relationships, access, goals, safety, or world state without requiring graphic danger.

dimensions.name: SOCIAL_RELATIONSHIP_COMPLEXITY
dimensions.description: Support trust, disagreement, rivalry, mentorship, competing interests, and mixed motives without adult melodrama.

dimensions.name: PREDICTABILITY_CHALLENGE
dimensions.description: Avoid obvious one-beat resolutions; allow wrong hypotheses, reversals, incomplete information, and earned payoff.

dimensions.name: WONDER_DISCOVERY
dimensions.description: Adventure-oriented episodes should offer places, systems, discoveries, mysteries, or experiences larger than ordinary daily-life simulation.

dimensions.name: LANGUAGE_READABILITY
dimensions.description: Use clear, natural language suitable for an independent 12-year-old reader. Story maturity must not depend on jargon.

required_story_capabilities: Meaningful protagonist role in the world
At least one non-trivial objective or unresolved question
Meaningful discovery or change in understanding
A real choice, strategic constraint, or consequential action
Persistent consequence or reusable world-state value
Adventure-oriented modes should include wonder, exploration, mystery, or extraordinary experience
reject_signals: Core premise is primarily pretend-play with toys, chores, or ordinary-room simulation unless explicitly requested
Difficult vocabulary is doing the work of making an otherwise young-child premise appear older
Problem resolves through one obvious attempt with no meaningful complication
Character mostly observes while adults or the world solve the important problem
Episode can be summarized as collect clue A, clue B, clue C with no reasoning change
Stakes are cosmetic and no persistent consequence can result
Mystery is solved before the character earns the relevant evidence
World can be swapped for any generic setting without changing the premise materially
language_rules: Technical terms are allowed when they serve the world or reasoning and can be understood in context
Do not infantilize dialogue or narration
Do not use vocabulary difficulty as a substitute for premise maturity
Keep exposition bounded and reveal information through action, observation, dialogue, or consequence where practical
safety_rules: Adventure tension is allowed without requiring graphic violence
Fear, danger, loss, rivalry, and uncertainty may be present when developmentally appropriate
Do not assume maturity requires darker or more violent content
Do not force romance, grief, betrayal, or trauma merely to make a story feel older
calibration_notes: A strong age-12 premise may involve systems failing, competing hypotheses, expedition planning, social disagreement, hidden history, evidence testing, or strategic risk.
A simple premise may still pass when deliberately selected for a calm/intimate mode, but should not be used as the default adventure ceiling.
Evaluate premise, narrative, conceptual, interest, and language maturity independently.

character.name: Deniz
character.origin_summary: Deniz grew up in Meridian Harbor apprenticing under a demanding mapmaker, driven to prove that patient observation can reveal what official charts miss.
character.current_role: apprentice cartographer under supervised but increasingly independent fieldwork

identity_anchors.statement: Deniz believes careful observation matters more than authority or bravado.
Deniz wants recognition earned through proof, not granted by rank.

core_drives.drive: Prove that rigorous observation reveals truths official maps miss.
Earn the right to chart beyond the home strait.

internal_tensions.side_b: pull toward reckless pursuit of a personally meaningful mystery
internal_tensions.description: Deniz's discipline is tested whenever a discovery brushes close to personal stakes.

immediate_desires: earn the right to chart beyond the home strait
find hard evidence others cannot dismiss
immediate_avoidances: being dismissed as a reckless or overconfident child surveyor

world.era: age of sail with precision mechanical navigation
world.habitat: a vast island chain divided by deep channels, storm belts and partially mapped outer seas
world.technology_level: sailing ships, mechanical clocks, optical instruments, printing presses and hand-built navigation devices
world.magic_level: rare, rule-bound geophysical phenomena associated with tides, magnetic stone and ancient infrastructure; no arbitrary spellcasting
world.summary: The Shattered Meridian is an archipelago civilization whose survival depends on maps. Most inner routes are well known, but outer charts disagree, old observatories stand on remote islands, drowned roads appear at extreme tides, and some navigation markers predate every living culture. The world rewards exploration, evidence and careful inference rather than effortless magic.
social_context: cartographers and navigators hold respected public roles
island councils depend on reliable sea routes
young apprentices may take meaningful expedition roles within established safety rules
merchant captains, fishers and scholars often disagree about what counts as trustworthy evidence
old folklore sometimes preserves real geographic information in distorted form
known_pressures: several navigation beacons no longer agree with official charts
outer-island routes are becoming economically important
storm season will eventually restrict long voyages
different groups have reasons to prefer different versions of the map
known_world_facts: Meridian Harbor is Deniz's home port and training base.
Beacon Ridge is part of the known inner navigation network.
The Drowned Causeway is known to appear only during rare low tides.
The Outer Mist Line marks the edge of reliable official charts.
An abandoned tide observatory exists on a distant mapped island.
Several beacon readings have recently become difficult to reconcile with official charts, but no accepted explanation exists yet.

main_saga_public.title: The Uncharted Disagreement
main_saga_public.goal: Discover why the Shattered Meridian's ancient navigation infrastructure and living tides no longer agree with official charts.
main_saga_public.stakes: Outer routes vital to island trade may become unsafe or unusable if the true cause of the discrepancies goes unaddressed.
main_saga_public.central_mystery: Something in the deep channels or the ancient beacon-markers is behaving in ways no known chart-making era can explain.

eligible_main_saga_milestones.summary: Deniz notices a beacon reading that disagrees with the official chart by a margin too large for instrument error.
eligible_main_saga_milestones.state_condition: Deniz has one documented anomaly and a working hypothesis that it is not simple mistake.
consequence_options: The friend becomes curious and offers to help verify.

active_side_sagas.premise: Deniz's practical-minded friend may want to pursue independent proof through experiments rather than surveying, creating friendly rivalry.
active_side_sagas.why_it_matters: Provides low-stakes roleplay and callback material outside the Main Saga.

creation_constraints: New entities must fit low-magic, rule-bound tidal/magnetic world logic.
New NPCs should have plausible reasons to intersect Deniz's apprentice life.
Do not contradict established hidden truths.

architect_raw_payload.title: The Angle That Wouldn't Match
architect_raw_payload.story_promise: Deniz must turn one suspicious reading into a defensible record before the tide window closes and the chance vanishes.
architect_raw_payload.protagonist_role: Apprentice surveyor conducting supervised but semi-independent beacon calibration checks.
architect_raw_payload.immediate_objective: Determine whether the beacon's drifting angle is real and tide-linked, or an instrument fault, before the tide turns.
architect_raw_payload.central_question: Is the beacon angle actually shifting with the tide, or is Deniz chasing a measurement mistake?
architect_raw_payload.stakes: A real anomaly could go unrecorded for a season, or Deniz could damage credibility by reporting too soon on thin evidence.
constraints: Limited daylight and tide window at Beacon Ridge
Only supervised access to the beacon instruments
Mentor evaluates methodology, not just conclusions
architect_raw_payload.opening_hook: Deniz logs a beacon angle that disagrees with the tide tables by too much to be rounding error, with the mentor already skeptical of 'ghost readings'.

logistics_plan.time_window: One low-to-rising tide cycle at Beacon Ridge, roughly three hours before the platform becomes unreachable and unmeasurable.
movement_constraints: Beacon Ridge access is only safe within the tide window; leaving and returning is not feasible mid-window
Harbor shipping logs can only be consulted after the tide window closes, since the harbor is a rowed crossing away
logistics_plan.feasibility_rationale: All measurement and decision beats occur at Beacon Ridge within the single tide cycle; the Harbor visit is deferred to after the window closes, so no impossible back-and-forth is required.

beats.purpose: Establish the anomaly and the ticking clock.
beats.character_action: Deniz logs the beacon's angle and checks it against the tide table.
beats.external_event: The angle is off by a margin the tables say should be impossible right now.
beats.new_information: One OBSERVED reading disagrees with the expected angle.
beats.escalation_delta: Introduces the single suspicious data point with no corroboration yet.
beats.state_change: Deniz now has one unexplained reading and a closing tide window.
beats.payoff_contribution: Sets up the core uncertainty the episode must resolve.

beats.purpose: Establish the mentor's evaluative stance and the stakes of being wrong.
beats.character_action: Deniz mentions the odd reading; the mentor asks for the methodology, not just the number.
beats.external_event: Mentor recalls past 'ghost readings' that turned out to be instrument drift.
beats.new_information: Mentor will judge Deniz on process, and single readings are treated as suspect by default.
beats.escalation_delta: Raises the bar for what counts as acceptable evidence.
beats.state_change: Deniz understands one reading will not be believed.
beats.payoff_contribution: Frames why Deniz must build a stronger evidence chain, not just repeat the claim.

beats.purpose: Rule out the simplest explanation without resolving the mystery.
beats.character_action: Deniz runs the standard instrument-control check used to detect a faulty sight-glass.
beats.external_event: The control check reads stable and normal, unlike the beacon angle.
beats.new_information: OBSERVED: the instrument itself is not malfunctioning.
beats.escalation_delta: Removes the easy 'broken tool' explanation, making the anomaly harder to dismiss but also harder to explain.
beats.state_change: Instrument error is ruled out; the mystery deepens rather than resolves.
beats.payoff_contribution: Strengthens the eventual evidence chain the reversal will rely on.

beats.purpose: Begin building a real, time-stamped observation series within the single session.
beats.character_action: Deniz takes timestamped angle readings every few minutes as the tide keeps rising, alongside repeated control checks.
beats.external_event: The tide visibly climbs against the marker posts while Deniz records each reading.
beats.new_information: OBSERVED: a short series of timestamped angle readings paired with tide height and a stable control reading.
beats.escalation_delta: Shifts from one anomaly to a small but real dataset, raising the possibility of a pattern.
beats.state_change: Deniz now holds multiple data points from one continuous session, not just one.
beats.payoff_contribution: This is the direct evidence the reversal will legitimately rest on.

beats.purpose: Tighten the window and force faster, riskier decisions.
beats.character_action: Deniz notices the safe platform time shrinking and must choose how many more readings to attempt.
beats.external_event: The tide crosses toward the point where the platform becomes unreachable, and light is fading.
beats.new_information: The dataset so far shows the angle shifting in the same direction as the rising tide, but only within this one session.
beats.escalation_delta: Time pressure now threatens to cut off further data collection entirely, not just slow it.
beats.state_change: Deniz must finalize methodology under a hard deadline, with no chance to redo this specific window today.
beats.payoff_contribution: Sharpens the coming decision between reporting now and attempting one more corroborating pass.

beats.purpose: Add a second, different kind of pressure: relational, not just physical.
beats.character_action: The mentor arrives to end the session and asks what Deniz intends to log.
beats.external_event: Mentor states that an unsupported claim will affect how future solo checks are supervised.
beats.new_information: The mentor's trust, not just the tide, is now on the line.
beats.escalation_delta: Changes the decision space by adding a reputational cost to any choice, not just a scheduling one.
beats.state_change: Deniz can no longer treat this as a private curiosity; it will become a formal log entry.
beats.payoff_contribution: Sets the stakes for the branch consequences in the decision point.

beats.purpose: Reinterpret the single-anomaly belief using the session's actual dataset.
beats.character_action: Deniz lines up the timestamps, tide heights, and control readings side by side.
beats.external_event: The angle has moved consistently in step with the rising tide across the whole session, while the control stayed flat.
beats.new_information: INFERRED: within this session, the drift tracks tide height rather than random error.
beats.escalation_delta: Converts 'one bad reading' into 'a bounded but real pattern,' which is a stronger but still limited claim.
beats.state_change: Deniz's working hypothesis shifts from possible error to a tide-linked trend worth logging, with recurrence still unproven.
beats.payoff_contribution: This bounded, evidence-traceable trend is what the decision and payoff will be built on.

beats.purpose: Force the choice between reporting the bounded trend now or spending the last minutes seeking independent corroboration.
beats.character_action: Deniz weighs the shrinking platform time against the strength of what has been recorded.
beats.external_event: The tide nears the safety cutoff the mentor has already flagged.
beats.new_information: No new data yet; this is the moment of choice, not a discovery.
beats.escalation_delta: The choice itself becomes the final escalation: act now or risk losing the window forever.
beats.state_change: Deniz commits to one branch, shaping what evidence and relationship state exist afterward.
beats.payoff_contribution: Determines which local payoff and mentor-relationship outcome the episode earns.

beats.purpose: Dramatize the chosen branch under real time and credibility pressure.
beats.character_action: Deniz either writes up the session's dataset methodically for the mentor, or scrambles to reset the sight-glass for one independent confirming pass before the cutoff.
beats.external_event: The mentor watches how Deniz handles the final minutes, judging method as promised.
beats.new_information: Depends on branch: either a clearly argued log entry, or a second independent reading (successful or not) taken against the clock.
beats.escalation_delta: All prior pressure (tide, trust, evidence) converges into one decisive action with no fallback.
beats.state_change: The mentor forms a concrete judgment of Deniz's methodology based on the executed branch.
beats.payoff_contribution: Produces the material the payoff and mentor-relationship shift are built from.

beats.purpose: Deliver a concrete, earned local resolution.
beats.character_action: Deniz secures a written log entry describing the session's bounded, tide-tracking trend and its open questions.
beats.external_event: The mentor signs off on the entry as provisional but methodologically sound, or flags it for follow-up depending on the branch.
beats.new_information: A dated record now exists describing an observed, session-bound tide-linked drift, with cause and recurrence explicitly unresolved.
beats.escalation_delta: Pressure resolves into a durable, if incomplete, result.
beats.state_change: first_discrepancy_logged becomes eligible; mentor's view of Deniz shifts based on branch chosen.
beats.payoff_contribution: Delivers the episode's local payoff: a defensible, logged anomaly and a changed mentor relationship.

beats.purpose: Open the forward question without resolving the Main Saga mystery.
beats.character_action: Deniz crosses to the harbor afterward and checks the shipping logs for the same period as promised.
beats.external_event: The logs remain silent on any delays, neither confirming nor denying the drift's real-world effect.
beats.new_information: The harbor's silence is neutral, not corroborating, leaving the wider cause of the disagreement open.
beats.escalation_delta: None; this beat closes the loop rather than escalating.
beats.state_change: A rumor about 'the ridge beacon problem' begins circulating among navigators who hear of the log entry.
beats.payoff_contribution: Seeds the Main Saga forward question while keeping this episode's payoff intact.

escalation_ladder: Instrument-control check rules out the easy explanation (broken tool), making the anomaly harder to dismiss.
Repeated timestamped readings turn one anomaly into a small dataset, raising the possibility of a real pattern.
The shrinking tide window threatens to cut off all further data collection, forcing urgency.
The mentor's arrival adds a reputational cost to every remaining choice, changing the decision space beyond simple timing.

reversal.prior_belief: The first odd reading is probably a single instrument or operator error, as the mentor initially suspects.

evidence.claim: The beacon angle disagreed with the tide table on the first reading.
The instrument's control check stayed stable while the beacon angle did not.
Across one continuous session, the beacon angle shifted in step with rising tide height while the control reading stayed flat.
Within this session, the drift tracks tide state rather than random measurement error.
This tide-linked behavior recurs on other tide cycles or has a systematic cause in the old navigation network.

reversal.reinterpretation: The anomaly is not a stray bad reading but a bounded, session-observed trend tracking tide height, elevating it above simple operator error.
reversal.inference_ceiling: This establishes only that the pattern held during this one session; it does not prove recurrence on other tides, long-term regularity, or any physical cause.
reversal.unresolved_after_reversal: Whether this tide-linked pattern happens every cycle, what causes it, and whether it connects to the ancient navigation network remain completely open.

decision_point.pressure: The tide is about to cut off Beacon Ridge access, and the mentor is waiting to see what Deniz will formally log.

branches.option: Report the bounded, session-observed trend immediately as a provisional log entry.
branches.immediate_action: Deniz writes up the timestamped dataset, control comparison, and honest limits, and presents it before time runs out.
branches.evidence_state_after_choice: One well-documented session of correlated readings, explicitly framed as unconfirmed beyond this cycle.
branches.cost_or_risk: The log may be judged thin since it lacks a second independent session; mentor may only grant cautious, conditional credit.
branches.relationship_or_access_effect: Mentor sees careful methodology and honest limits, shifting toward cautious respect even without full proof.
branches.climax_requirement: Climax must show Deniz constructing a rigorous, honestly bounded argument under time pressure, not overclaiming.
branches.local_payoff_if_earned: A dated, methodologically sound log entry exists and is provisionally accepted, with the physical cause still open for the Saga.

branches.option: Spend the final minutes resetting the instrument to attempt one independent confirming reading before the cutoff.
branches.immediate_action: Deniz recalibrates the sight-glass and races to take a second, separately-set reading before the platform becomes unsafe.
branches.evidence_state_after_choice: Either a genuinely independent confirming reading is obtained, or time runs out with no new data and the window lost.
branches.cost_or_risk: Risk of losing the entire window with nothing gained, or of rushing the reset and introducing a real instrument error.
branches.relationship_or_access_effect: Mentor's reaction depends on outcome: a clean independent confirmation earns strong trust, while a failed rushed attempt may cost future solo access.
branches.climax_requirement: Climax must show Deniz executing a technically sound recalibration under real deadline pressure, using the control-check skill established earlier.
branches.local_payoff_if_earned: If successful, a stronger two-session-equivalent log entry; if it fails, a harder lesson about overreach and a more skeptical mentor stance.

decision_point.what_is_unknown: Whether the mentor will accept a session-bound trend as sufficient, and whether a rushed second attempt would succeed or backfire.

architect_raw_payload.climax: Under the closing tide window and the mentor's watching judgment, Deniz executes the chosen branch — either building an honest, rigorous log argument from the session's dataset, or racing to recalibrate for a genuinely independent second reading — using the instrument-control method and tide observations established earlier, with no new unexplained fact introduced.
architect_raw_payload.local_payoff: Deniz secures a dated, methodologically defensible log entry describing a real, session-observed tide-linked drift, with the mentor's stance shifted according to the branch earned, while the physical cause remains an open Saga question.
architect_raw_payload.forward_hook: The harbor's shipping logs stay silent on any confirming disruption, leaving the wider question of why the beacon disagrees with the charts — and whether the pattern repeats — unresolved as a rumor begins to spread among navigators.

persistent_outcome_candidates.description: A session-bound, tide-correlated beacon drift observation, explicitly bounded in scope.
persistent_outcome_candidates.commit_condition: Episode delivers the reversal beats with the specified evidence chain intact.

persistent_outcome_candidates.description: Mentor's assessment of Deniz shifts toward cautious respect, continued skepticism, or renewed doubt depending on the branch and its outcome.
persistent_outcome_candidates.commit_condition: Decision branch is dramatized through to its climax consequence.

persistent_outcome_candidates.description: A dated logbook entry documenting the anomaly becomes a reusable reference.
persistent_outcome_candidates.commit_condition: Payoff beat is reached with the log entry actually written and reviewed.

persistent_outcome_candidates.description: Harbor navigators begin discussing 'the ridge beacon problem.'
persistent_outcome_candidates.commit_condition: Tag beat occurs with the log entry known to have circulated.

persistent_outcome_candidates.description: first_discrepancy_logged milestone becomes eligible for commit.
persistent_outcome_candidates.commit_condition: Payoff beat delivers a logged, evidence-traceable anomaly meeting the milestone's state_condition.

completion_evidence: A documented, timestamped dataset from one session showing angle correlated with tide height, distinct from instrument error.
A concrete decision beat where Deniz chooses between reporting now and seeking independent corroboration, with dramatized consequence.
A resulting log entry that the mentor reviews and responds to, establishing the anomaly as logged rather than dismissed.
Explicit narrative acknowledgment that recurrence and cause remain unresolved beyond this session.

anti_repetition_signature.core_problem_shape: Single ambiguous data point must be strengthened into defensible evidence within a hard, non-repeatable time window.
anti_repetition_signature.primary_activity: Field measurement, instrument-control testing, and timestamped comparative observation.
anti_repetition_signature.main_location_pattern: Single-location time-critical fieldwork (Beacon Ridge) followed by a deferred, lower-stakes cross-check location (Meridian Harbor).
anti_repetition_signature.climax_shape: Branch-dependent execution under closing deadline: rigorous write-up versus risky recalibration attempt.
anti_repetition_signature.distinct_from_recent_episodes_because: No prior episodes exist; this establishes the baseline evidence-and-trust pattern the Saga will later complicate.

writer_rules: Do not have any character or event confirm the tidal pattern recurs beyond this single session.
Do not resolve the physical cause of the drift; keep it an open Saga question.
Do not let the harbor shipping logs corroborate or contradict the anomaly; their silence must remain neutral.
Do not pre-decide which decision branch Deniz takes; dramatize the choice as genuinely uncertain.
Do not introduce any new unexplained fact at the climax; use only evidence and skills established in earlier beats.
Keep all reversal claims within the certainty levels specified (OBSERVED vs INFERRED vs HYPOTHESIS).
Do not treat first_discrepancy_logged as canonically complete; only show it becoming eligible.
Do not have Deniz travel between Beacon Ridge and Meridian Harbor during the tide window; the harbor visit happens only after.
